title: Ground truth on the real execution device — read-only baseline
context: Arena already executed every local verifier in its own coordinator sandbox (Linux, Node v22.22.3) BEFORE the Priti AI change, and all were green: check-syntax 41 files / 0 errors, health-check 95 passed 0 failed, e2e-test 134 passed 0 failed (default store AND PJS_STORAGE=json), agent-team-check PASS, agent-storage doctor PASS with a 12-entry intact hash chain, worktree clean. This batch is about proving the same on the preserved current tree.

Arena's sandbox CANNOT reach the production host: TLS to panikajeevansathi.onrender.com:443 is reset (curl exit 35 SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, node fetch ECONNRESET, both inside ~75 ms) while github.com returns 200 from the same box. That is coordinator egress, not evidence of an outage — only T-07 on the device can decide it.

reports/agents/render-employee-latest.json still records 2 'production failures': /register.html and /forgot-password.html returning 404. Arena checked the tree: no page, no route and no link references either path (registration lives in /login.html?tab=register, reset lives in /reset-password.html), and the check that produced them is a hardcoded guess list in scripts/render-doctor.mjs. It is reported, NOT fixed, in this batch.

Two further defects are queued for a later batch and must not be patched here: scripts/agent-storage-cycle.mjs exits 1 when a worker is only BLOCKED (0 FAIL), and reports/agents/zero-survival-latest.json is a 268-byte stub from a run whose network probes never succeeded.

Termux is the only place some of these answers exist: real Android filesystem behaviour, real outbound network, the device's own Node build. Anything Arena could not measure is exactly what this batch measures.

base_commit 538beebd21e2 is the commit that SHIPS this protocol (ops/TERMUX-BATCH-PROTOCOL.md, ops/batches/*, scripts/termux-batch.mjs, package.json batch scripts) on top of the app-code pin 8ef92b7b9c62. T-02 therefore pins the RUNTIME code (server.js, lib/, public/, agents/) to 8ef92b7b9c62 explicitly, so tooling commits can never mask or fake app-code drift; the runner also records head_matches_base and the validator prints any head drift as a warning.

head_policy is "descendant-ok-with-app-code-pin": Termux must be AT or AHEAD of base_commit (a pure fast-forward pull). Being ahead is only forgiven because T-02 itself asserts server.js/lib/public/agents are byte-identical to app pin 8ef92b7b9c62 — a validator pass without that task passing is treated as a violation, not a warning.
Recut after owner handoff: the 143-line Priti AI change in public/assets/js/app.js is intentional application work and is PRESERVED. It is the new approved UI baseline.

The old fingerprint 5469d2287361… was the pre-Priti main. BATCH-01 no longer pins it as the current truth; T-01 captures the real device fingerprint and regenerates reports/ui-baseline-body.md5 from the preserved tree.
This batch is read-only against public/**. The only tracked file that may differ from base is public/assets/js/app.js; T-02 and T-10 assert that and nothing else.
no D1 write, no migration, no deploy, no git push, no destructive git command is attempted or allowed by this batch.
rules: Execute one task at a time in the printed order. Do not reorder, merge, split or skip a task.
Never write PASS for a command that did not exit 0. Paste the exit code and output you actually saw.
Blocked means: name the exact missing dependency (env var, binary, permission, host) in remaining_dependency, then continue with the next task.

This batch is read-only. No edits to server.js, lib/, public/, agents/, scripts/. No git add/commit/push, no deploy, no database or .env writes, no password or private-message access, no email, no social posting.
Do not install anything (pkg/npm install) inside a task. A missing tool is a BLOCKED result naming that tool, not a setup job.
public/** must stay byte-identical to the fingerprint above. If any check reports drift, stop and report the file and its hash.
Use the runner so evidence is captured, not retyped: `node scripts/termux-batch.mjs run BATCH-01`. Then send ops/batches/BATCH-01.results.json and .results.md back to Arena.
Arena validates with `node scripts/termux-batch.mjs validate BATCH-01` and only then issues BATCH-02. A rejected result batch is re-run, never argued into acceptance.

tasks.title: Approved UI baseline capture + device capability truth
tasks.objective: Record the device's real capability record AND capture the approved UI baseline: Node version, git/curl, free disk, HEAD/branch, worktree, and the ACTUAL sha256 fingerprint of the preserved public/ tree (which includes the approved Priti AI change). The command writes ops/batches/BATCH-01.baseline.json and regenerates reports/ui-baseline-body.md5 from the current tree. It never modifies, deletes, restores or cleans any public/** file.

actions: capture the current public UI baseline under explicit owner approval
read files; run read-only commands
print versions

verify.expect: exit 0 AND the output says the approved UI baseline was captured, names the baseline file ops/batches/BATCH-01.baseline.json, confirms reports/ui-baseline-body.md5 was regenerated, and confirms public/** was untouched. The new fingerprint is the real sha256 of the preserved device tree, NOT a value Arena guessed.
verify.blocked_reason: live host probes were attempted but this network refused them

tasks.expected_report: The captured fingerprint + file count, the baseline file path, and an explicit 'public/** untouched' statement. Also report node version, git/curl presence, disk, HEAD/branch and worktree state.
tasks.stop_condition: If the command cannot write the baseline file (e.g. read-only ops/batches/), record BLOCKED naming the exact path/permission. If public/** is reported as modified by the baseline command, STOP: the tool has a bug and must not continue.

tasks.title: Tree integrity at the approved app state
tasks.objective: Verify the app code on the device is exactly the approved state. Two separate claims: (a) under server.js, lib/, public/ and agents/ the ONLY tracked working-tree change is public/assets/js/app.js (the approved 143-line Priti AI feature); nothing else in app code is locally modified (untracked backups are ignored by --untracked-files=no so they are not treated as app code; scripts/ is tooling and outside this app-code pin); (b) committed runtime code between base 0a273a27e24a9efdbe9c275b4fd948191eded2ae and HEAD is byte-identical, so tooling commits can never mask or fake app-code drift. Syntax and the agent-team safety config must both be green. The whitespace gate is scoped to code/tooling paths on purpose.

actions: read files
run the repo's own syntax + team checks
verify the single approved app-code change
forbidden: editing any file to make a check pass

require_empty: git diff --name-only 0a273a27e24a9efdbe9c275b4fd948191eded2ae HEAD -- server.js lib public agents
git diff --check 0a273a27e24a9efdbe9c275b4fd948191eded2ae HEAD -- server.js lib public agents scripts package.json
verify.expect: check-syntax prints '41 checked, 0 with syntax errors'; agent-team-check prints 'AGENT TEAM CHECK: PASS'; app-diff-verify prints 'APP CODE DIFF OK' and exits 0; and the committed runtime diff + whitespace gate each print NOTHING. app-diff-verify is the machine check that the only allowed tracked app-code change is public/assets/js/app.js (the approved Priti AI feature).

tasks.expected_report: The three PASS lines, the exact output of app-diff-verify (normally the single approved public/assets/js/app.js line), and confirmation the two committed checks printed nothing.
tasks.stop_condition: If app-diff-verify names any file OTHER than public/assets/js/app.js, or the committed runtime diff prints a file: STOP the batch, paste `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no -- server.js lib public agents` and `git log --oneline -3`, and wait for Arena. Never 'fix' it by editing, stashing, checking out or resetting.

tasks.title: Live production reachability from a real network (the one thing Arena's sandbox cannot answer)
tasks.objective: From Termux's own network, measure the live service: /api/health body and status, / , /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, the old cPanel host, and the actual route list discovered from served HTML. tasks.title: Broken internal-link audit against the device copy (manual — pipelines need a shell)
tasks.objective: Extract every internal href actually present in public/*.html, and confirm each one resolves to a real file (or a documented /api/ route). This is the on-device confirmation of Arena's finding that no page links to /register.html or /forgot-password.html — i.e. that the 2 'production failures' in reports/agents/render-employee-latest.json come from a hardcoded guess list in scripts/render-doctor.mjs, not from a broken UI. Audit only: no HTML edit is approved in this batch.

actions: run the listed shell pipeline
read public/*.html

manual_commands: grep -rhoE 'href="/[^"]+"' public/*.html | sed -E 's/.*href="//; s/[?#].*//; s/"$//' | sort -u > /tmp/pjs-links.txt
while read -r p; do case "$p" in /api/*) continue;; esac; [ -f "public$p" ] || echo "UNRESOLVED $p"; done < /tmp/pjs-links.txt
verify.instructions: Run the four lines by hand in the repo root on Termux. Command 2 must print NOTHING for a PASS. Paste all four outputs (including the empty one) into ops/batches/BATCH-01.manual-template.json — set status to PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED, put the real exit codes from `echo $?` into action_performed, then re-run the batch with `node scripts/termux-batch.mjs run BATCH-01 --import ops/batches/BATCH-01.manual-template.json`. The runner will refuse to invent this result: if you do not import it, T-09 is recorded BLOCKED.
verify.expect: zero UNRESOLVED lines, and the wc -l count of distinct static internal hrefs equals 18 (Arena measured 18 on the pinned tree: /admin.html, /assets/css/app.css, /assets/img/favicon.svg, /contact.html, /dashboard.html, /edit-profile.html, /index.html, /interests.html, /login.html, /matches.html, /messages.html, /notifications.html, /privacy.html, /profile.html, /search.html, /settings.html, /shortlist.html, /terms.html). A different count on the device means a different tree — say so in the evidence. This pipeline only sees hrefs written literally in HTML; links built in JS (e.g. /profile.html?id=) are covered by T-03/T-04, not here.

tasks.expected_report: The exact output of commands 1-4, the count from wc -l, and an explicit 'UNRESOLVED count: 0' (or the list). Include the sentence that no public/** file was modified.
tasks.stop_condition: If a genuine UNRESOLVED link appears: report file + href and stop there. Public UI changes need the owner's explicit approval, so proposing a patch is allowed but applying one is not.
